scope: Five selected historical NASA successful lunar soft landings for educational visualization. Not a complete history of all countries or Moon missions.

coordinate_convention.longitude: East positive [0, 360); west longitude converted by 360 - west
coordinate_convention.global_frame_note: Apollo points are LRO-derived positions in lunar Mean Earth/Polar Axis DE421; Surveyor 1 is an approximate historical location. Check alignment with any global Moon texture or 3D mesh.
coordinate_convention.regional_dem_coverage_note: The professional polar LOLA DEM covers about 80-90 degrees south. None of these historical landings lies within that coverage.

missions.name: Surveyor 1
missions.coordinate_frame: NSSDCA historical selenographic (approximate; not independently cross-registered to DE421)
missions.achievement: First successful U.S. robotic soft landing on the Moon.
missions.description: Surveyor 1 demonstrated a controlled, gentle robotic landing and returned photographs of the lunar surface.
missions.educational_question: Why did engineers need to test soft landings before sending astronauts?
missions.coordinate_note: NASA NSSDCA lists 2.45° S, 316.79° E (43.21° W). A NASA Science page instead states approximately 2.46° S, 43.32° W. Treat this historical site marker as approximate; do not claim meter-scale accuracy.

missions.name: Apollo 11
missions.coordinate_frame: Moon Mean Earth/Polar Axis (DE421), LRO-derived Lunar Module location
missions.achievement: First human landing on the Moon.
missions.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed in the Sea of Tranquility while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.
missions.educational_question: Why did the Apollo 11 crew choose a relatively smooth landing region?

missions.name: Apollo 12
missions.coordinate_frame: Moon Mean Earth/Polar Axis (DE421), LRO-derived Lunar Module location
missions.achievement: Precision landing near the earlier Surveyor 3 spacecraft.
missions.description: Apollo 12 landed close to Surveyor 3, enabling astronauts to inspect hardware that had spent years on the Moon.
missions.educational_question: How does a precision landing help scientists plan future missions?
missions.coordinate_note: NASA NSSDCA lists the Lunar Module at 23.4219° W, stored as 336.5781° E.

missions.name: Apollo 15
missions.coordinate_frame: Moon Mean Earth/Polar Axis (DE421), LRO-derived Lunar Module location
missions.achievement: First crewed lunar mission to use the Lunar Roving Vehicle.
missions.description: Apollo 15 explored the Hadley–Apennine landscape using a lunar rover to reach geological sites beyond walking distance.
missions.educational_question: How did the lunar rover change what astronauts could investigate?

missions.name: Apollo 17
missions.coordinate_frame: Moon Mean Earth/Polar Axis (DE421), LRO-derived Lunar Module location
missions.achievement: Final crewed lunar landing of the Apollo program, including geologist Harrison Schmitt.
missions.description: Apollo 17 investigated the Taurus–Littrow valley, collecting rocks and volcanic materials to study lunar history.
missions.educational_question: What can a rock sample reveal about the Moon’s ancient volcanoes?
